sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › Climatic change and climatic regions - world, India and Andhra Pradesh › Climate action plans - NAPCC missions and AP SAPCC
bullets: NAPCC launched 30 June 2008; 8 missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge (IYB 2026; APP).

ES 2025-26: adaptation spending 5.6% of GDP (FY22); SAPCCs shifted from mitigation plans (2010-15) to district-level, risk-based adaptation plans (2020 onwards); Odisha was the first state with a SAPCC (2010) (IYB).

sections.topic: Climate change · Impacts
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › Climate change - evidence, natural and anthropogenic causes, global warming, IPCC assessments, impacts › Impacts
bullets: Sea level: thermal expansion plus ice melt; uninhabited South Pacific islets Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea submerged in 1999; Kiribati, Tuvalu at risk (APP).

Coral bleaching: the 1.2 degC threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse is already crossed; beyond ~2 degC parts of the Amazon may turn savanna (UN brief, LENSD 24 Jun 2026). Reefs need 15+ years to recover (APP).
Oceans and species: acidity up 30% since the Industrial Revolution (CDI); up to 25% of mountain species face extinction (AR6, CDI).

Extremes and agriculture: India 2025 - 4,419 deaths and 17.4 million ha of crops damaged by extreme weather (WMO 2025, CDI); buffalo milk yields in Haryana's trans-Gangetic plains hit by warming (TH, 6 Jul 2026).
Disease spread: warmer, wetter conditions widen the range of vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue.

sections.topic: Mobility through reservation, education, migration
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

sections.topic: Services sector · Services exports
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-1 › Services sector - growth, composition and contribution to GDP and employment › Services exports - software, business services, India's share and targets
bullets: India is the world's 7th-largest services exporter. Its share of global services trade rose from 2% (2005) to 4.3% (2024) (ES 2025-26). IYB 2026, using WTO data, ranks India 8th with the same 4.3% share.
Services exports were USD 387.5 bn in 2024-25 (+13.6%) against imports of USD 198.7 bn, a steady surplus (IYB 2026).
In FY2025-26 services exports grew 15.3%. Software and business services made up 77.8% of them (APPCA, Jun 2026). CAGR was 14% over FY23-FY25, about double the pre-pandemic 7.6% (ES).
Earlier target (asked by APPSC): India's share of world services exports was to reach 4.2% by 2022. The government's overall export target is USD 1 trillion (LENS, Jul 2025).

India's crude basket averaged $82.04/bbl in July 2026 (vs $70.95 a year earlier). Brent was around $91.84 in Aug 2026 (TH, 19 Aug 2026).

India = 3rd largest energy consumer and 3rd largest oil consumer (APPCA 2026); imports ~88% of crude (LENS daily, Aug 2026).

sections.topic: MPC composition
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Monetary Policy Committee and the flexible inflation targeting framework › MPC composition - members, appointment, casting vote, meetings, quorum
bullets: RBI Governor: How Chairperson (ex officio); casting vote on a tie
One RBI officer: How Nominated by the RBI Central Board
A statutory body under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, created by the 2016 amendment. It fixes the policy repo rate needed to hit the inflation target, and its decisions bind RBI.
Each member has one vote and decisions are by majority. The Governor has a casting vote in a tie. The MPC must meet at least 4 times a year; in practice it meets bi-monthly (six times).

Latest decisions: on 5 Aug 2026 the MPC voted unanimously to hold the repo at 5.25% with a neutral stance (TH, 6 Aug 2026). The minutes of the August meeting point to a likely hike: headline inflation averaged 3.93% so far this year and core inflation is projected at 4.3% for 2026-27 (TH, 20 Aug 2026).

EBLR: from 1 Oct 2019, new floating-rate personal/retail and MSE loans must be linked to an external benchmark. Options: repo, 3-month or 6-month T-bill yield, or an FBIL-published rate (APP).
Trap: SLR and CRR are set by RBI, not by banks; MCLR is each bank's internal benchmark.
PLR: From 1994; Key point Rate for the best borrowers, set by each bank

Draft RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026: proposed to take effect from 1 April 2027. It covers banks, RRBs, co-operative banks, AIFIs and NBFCs/HFCs. Floating-rate personal and MSME loans stay tied to an external benchmark, with interest on the daily reducing balance (LENSD, 14 Aug 2026).

bullets: Four Deputy Governors - two from RBI ranks, one commercial banker, one economist (monetary policy). Current: Rohit Jain (appointed May 2026, replacing T. Rabi Sankar), Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta, S. C. Murmu (TH, 3 May 2026).
Shaktikanta Das (2018-2024): Note Gave the "Seven Ages of India's Monetary Policy" speech (2020) [GK for tenure]
Sanjay Malhotra (since Dec 2024): Note Current Governor (TH 2026); chairs the MPC and the Payments Regulatory Board [GK for start date]
Central Board of Directors: 21 members, appointed by the Government of India under the RBI Act; directors hold office for 4 years.
RBI accounting year: April-March since 2020-21; earlier it ran July-June .

sections.topic: Inflation · Control measures
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures › Control measures - monetary, fiscal, supply-side
bullets: Monetary (RBI): Tools Raise repo rate, CRR, OMO sales, anchor expectations; repo held at 5.25% (Aug 2026) with an October hike expected (TH, 8 Aug, 16 Sep 2026)

Supply-side: Tools OMSS (Domestic) - FCI sells wheat and rice at fixed prices; Price Stabilisation Fund buffer of pulses and onions; subsidised Bharat Atta, Bharat Rice, Bharat Dal (Bharat Chana Dal from July 2023 at ₹60/kg)
APPSC-G1 2024 key credited the Bharat Atta initiative with easing prices.
Monetary: Examples Raise repo rate, CRR; sell securities through OMOs; tighten liquidity
Limitation: the repo rate is a demand-side tool and cannot fix supply shocks such as onion prices or crude oil (CDI).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › Andhra Pradesh - climate, rainfall regions, cyclone vulnerability, drought-prone areas › Rain-shadow and drought-prone zone
bullets: Rayalaseema lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and the Karnataka/Telangana highlands, so it gets little SW-monsoon rain (CDI). Anantapur is the lowest-rainfall district.
Chronic droughts hit Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam when the NE monsoon fails; groundwater depletion adds to this (CDI).

2026: a deficient year. The SW monsoon deficit reached 51.2% (1 Jun-25 Aug), with all 28 districts deficient. Causes: El Nino subsidence, and all seven low-pressure systems forming at the head of the Bay (CDCA Aug 2026).

sections.topic: Women’s Political Representation and Reservation
sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Polity › #76 · Women’s Political Representation and Reservation
bullets: Women's political reservation was first constitutionally institutionalized through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992.
Women's reservation in the House of the People covers seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi covers Scheduled Caste-reserved seats.
Not less than one-third of the total seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 243D(2) must be reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The mandatory sub-quota for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women within Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats is one-third.

sections.topic: Constitutional Articles on Social Rights

bullets: Article 14 concerns women.
Article 14 concerns caste.
Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
Article 15(4) provides special provisions for Scheduled Castes.
Article 46 provides for the promotion of Scheduled Caste interests.

sections.topic: Purity-pollution and cultural traits of caste
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Caste - features, theories of origin, varna-jati distinction › Purity-pollution and cultural traits of caste
bullets: Dumont: hierarchy rests on the pure vs impure; *Homo Hierarchicus* vs *Homo Aequalis* (CDX).
McKim Marriott: the interactional approach, ranking castes by exchange of "coded substances" (food, water, services) (CDX).
Traits: commensal taboos, the pollution-by-touch idea, untouchability, Sanskritic rituals (CDX, APP).
Dipankar Gupta counters Dumont: castes are discrete communities and "difference" is not "hierarchy" (CDX).
